The silence of the lighthouse is not an absence of sound, but a presence of memory. As the tide rolls in and out, it seems to carry the weight of the past with it. The iron gallery, once a structure of strength, now feels like a skeleton of time. To stand before it is to feel the passage of centuries pressing gently against the ground.

The keeper's cottage, though cold, holds a warmth that is the warmth of habit. The tin of tea, its label faded, reminds us that even the smallest things can become significant when we stop to notice them. The slate roof, weathered by the elements, has become a canvas for the sky. The windows, set deep into the walls, seem to look out at the sea as if they are trying to see something beyond the horizon.

Maps of the coast, drawn by hand, are more than just lines on paper. They are stories written in the language of the tide. Each inlet, each cliff, each change in the water's colour holds a memory. The patience required to measure these things is a lesson in mindfulness. It teaches us to resist the urge to rush and to appreciate the small details.
